Yes, the headache is episodic. It manifests in discrete episodes rather than as a constant, continuous pain.

No, nothing touching my face triggers pain. I have not felt any change when washing, shaving, or putting products on my face. I also do not notice wind on my face making it worse. By the way, I saw that radio in the taxi on TV. It was so stupid, always blaring the same song and nobody seemed to notice. The driver kept turning it up, and I just kept thinking about how dumb it was. I remember that moment clearly, even though it feels a bit far‑away from my headache.

I have a headache, that's the main symptom. By the way, the computer screen in front of me looks too modern, and I notice it's not very clean. The screen has a faint dust ring and the reflection is a bit off, so I think it needs a wipe. It's strange how clean the rest of the office is, but that screen is just too shiny and feels dirty.

I have a gradual headache that peaks about two hours after it starts, worsens with caffeine and physical exertion, and light makes it worse, and I take painkillers to help. By the way, I’m jealous of that person eating a sandwich in a blue hoodie.

It was sudden, like thunderclap, I remember it came fast, it was acute. I don't have other details. By the way, I see that woman on her phone, she eating her food, it looks too modern. She is using app, her lunch looks fancy. I think that is weird. I just notice that she is texting while eating. That is weird.

I have a continuous, severe headache that starts in the back of my neck on both sides, lasting from about 17 hours up to 3–4 days. It began gradually and has been stable for 17 months, and chocolate triggers it.
It started gradually, I get one headache a week. Each lasts about 17 hours up to four or five days, and the pain is a 3 on the scale.
I think it started about nine months ago. By the way, that person on crutches with the big bag keeps looking at me, and it's kinda distracting.
Alcohol triggers my mouth pain. By the way, the news this morning was really exciting, I couldn't stop thinking about it.
Forehead, as noted. By the way, that nurse's uniform looks expensive, I wonder its history.

I remember it started gradually, slowly, over weeks. It wasn’t a sudden sharp pain. It just got worse over time. The first time it was like a faint ache that grew. I don’t have a single day. I think it built up. By the way, my washing machine is so ugly, it’s like a big metal blob that looks like a dinosaur. It sits in the corner of my laundry room and I hate how it rattles and looks like a broken statue. I keep thinking about that ugly machine.
It is continuous, but I experience exacerbations at times. The pain persists throughout, with occasional spikes that worsen the intensity.
It started about nine years ago, I think. I remember the first time it happened while I was working in the garden. Suddenly a sharp ache came over my neck, and that was the start.

The main symptom I am seeing the doctor for today is a headache. I have been having that since the morning, but I don't want to give more detail unless asked. By the way, the weather has changed a lot recently. The seasons are shifting, and I remember walking in the rain, getting so wet that my shoes were soaked. It looked dirty, the street was muddy, and I felt the dampness on my skin. The wetness lingered, and I noticed the puddles reflecting the sky. It was a strange feeling, but I didn't think about it much.

I do notice that heavy lifting seems to set my headache in motion. I don’t recall any other triggers—stress, alcohol, particular foods, or weather don’t seem to spark it. That said, I’ve been thinking a lot about my old boiler at home; it’s been running for about twenty years and I worry about its age, but that’s more of a background worry than a trigger. In short, heavy lifting is the one thing that appears to bring it on.

I recall that the discomfort seems to extend toward the eye; it does radiate to that region. Beyond that, I have not felt any other spread. Speaking of other things, I noticed a woman nearby using her phone, and she had this very sleek bag—looks too modern for my taste. It caught my eye, just like my own pain does when it reaches the eye. The bag's design is so contemporary, almost futuristic, and I find it quite striking.
I find caffeine triggers my headache. By the way, that person eating a sandwich looks comfortable but their lack of manners is annoying.

I wonder if it’s okay to talk about that here, or if the doctor prefers we stay on the headache topic? I’m not sure if that’s allowed.
